body: I think the second option should be avoided, as we want to conform to ECS fields as much as possible, and `constant_keyword` is part of that (the newer scheme assumes a data stream only ever contains a single value for a `dataset`.

body: If that's the case, we really ought to consider rolling back https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/pull/117933, because that introduces a second value. If we don't roll that back, it is always possible that the data stream has two values for this field, even if we come up with a way to prevent any individual index from having no more than one value.

If we roll back, we need to hold 9.0.0 for it. Otherwise if someone sets up a new 9.0.0 cluster, gets the post-#117933 value, then upgrades to 9.0.1 where it's been reverted, they'll have the same problem.

issue.title: Rename deprecation index template

labels.name: auto-backport

repository.name: elasticsearch
repository.description: Free and Open Source, Distributed, RESTful Search Engine

issue.body:
The dataset name for the deprecation logs index was previously renamed from `deprecation.elasticsearch` to `elasticsearch.deprecation` in order to follow the pattern of `product.group`. The deprecation index template, however, was not updated. This causes indexing errors once upgraded to 9.0 due to the dataset name having changed on a constant_keyword field. In order to avoid that mismatch, this commit renames the deprecation indexing datastream to match the dataset name. The old template is kept in place, but marked as deprecated, so that any deprecation logs written during upgrading to 9.x will continue to be indexed into the old datastream.

closes #125445
